game.name: TIDEBREAKERS
game.title: TIDEBREAKERS
game.pitch:
A mobile-first, stylized 3D survival adventure on a flooded Earth, built for iPhone Safari and Home Screen install.
The look is Waterworld-inspired ocean survival: everything salvaged, patched and fought over, scrap atolls and outposts
in an immense dark sea, and **green means alive**: living plants are the rarest, most valuable thing in the world
(see `docs/waterworld-pass/`, and `docs/grimy-pass/` for the weathering foundation).
Civilization is under the sea. You start in a patchwork skiff at

collections.doc:
The sloop's upgrade models (GITCRAFT TIDEBREAKERS 3D package), each modelled at its socket's origin. An owned
upgrade mounts as a child of its socket_* node; if its file failed to load, the code-built part is drawn instead.

unclassified.doc:
The rest of the Trimaran's upgrades (MeshCraft, creative/3d-sloop/upgrades), modelled in the sloop's own frame and
laid out together so that none overlaps another, the helm, the wheel or the captain with everything fitted (an
overlap audit in Blender checks every pair, with the moving parts swept through their range). Static nodes join
the ship's batched kit mesh; `pivot` is a moving part the game turns. `roof` nodes stand on the cabin roof.

missions.title: First Voyage
missions.brief: Drag the wheel (bottom-left) toward where you want to go. Push further to raise more sail.

objectives.hint: Drag the wheel (bottom-left) toward where you want to go. Push further to raise more sail.
Head north, away from the raft docks, into open water.

objectives.text: Sail to the atoll to the west
objectives.hint: Follow the gold marker. That’s Turtle Atoll, the top of a drowned hill.
Slow down close to shore and tap ANCHOR.
Tap GO ASHORE to wade onto the beach.
Something is glinting on the south beach.
Open MAPS and read the clue carefully.
Use the landmarks on the map. Your shovel will tell you when the sand feels loose.
Board your skiff, raise anchor and sail home. Dock at the raft pier.
Open the harbor and visit Pip the Trader.
Tap CATALOG to see what you’ve found.

objectives.text: Buy your first upgrade from Marlo
objectives.hint: Visit the Shipwright. The Canvas Mainsail is a fine start.
Follow the Captain’s Log: salvage, upgrade, explore further.

places.name: Driftholm
places.blurb: Rafts lashed to the last hill of the old harbour town. Home.

places.name: Turtle Atoll
places.blurb: A ring of dead coral around the top of a drowned hill. Shaped like a turtle, if you squint. Something green was seen here.

places.name: Lantern Rock
places.blurb: The old coast light. The coast is gone. The light still watches.

places.name: Gull Shoal
places.blurb: A ring of breakers guards the wreck of the trawler Wren. Only a strong hull gets through.

places.name: Canopy Rise
places.blurb: The last hilltop with soil on it. The gardeners are long gone, but behind their scrap walls the last tree still stands.

places.name: Driftholm
places.blurb: Rafts lashed to the last hill of the old harbour. Your vault and your people are here.

places.name: Rooftop Hollow
places.blurb: Forty fishers living on the roof of a drowned apartment block. They trade fish for anything.

places.name: Rig Helios
places.blurb: An oil platform turned market. The flare still burns. Engines, radar and hard bargains.

places.name: The Sunken Tower
places.blurb: The top four floors of an office block. Somebody already took the chairs.

places.name: The Box Yard
places.blurb: Four shipping containers that floated in on a storm and never left.

places.name: Hollow Underfloors
places.blurb: The flooded floors under Rooftop Hollow. The fishers let you dive if you share.

places.name: Meridian Plaza
places.blurb: The tallest roof of Old Meridian. The view is the whole drowned city.

places.name: Broadcast Spire
places.blurb: The antenna still hums when the wind is right. Heavy gear down there.

places.name: The Leaning Block
places.blurb: It has been falling over for fifty years. Very slowly.

places.name: Helios Lower Deck
places.blurb: The flooded pump deck. Crude still seeps from the old lines.

places.name: Hull of the Meridian Star
places.blurb: A supertanker, standing on her stern. Rustfang raiders call it theirs.

places.name: Graveyard Boxes
places.blurb: Boxes spilled from the tanker when she went down.

places.name: The Meridian Spire
places.blurb: The tallest thing left in the world. At the top: the chart everybody whispers about.

places.name: Rustfang Hold
places.blurb: A raider atoll of scrap walls and a hull-plate gate. The scorch marks are from the last people who tried.

places.name: The Last Tree
places.blurb: Green. Actual green, on the hilltop, behind scrap walls. Someone fought to keep it alive.

worlds.name: The Drift
worlds.blurb: Silted shallows over a drowned county. Rooftops, dead reefs and rumours.

worlds.name: The Sunken Reach
worlds.blurb: Open swell over the old cities. Towers, rigs and raiders.

worlds.name: The Stormwall
worlds.blurb: A storm that never ends. Something tall stands inside it.

characters.name: Juno Vale
characters.desc: “You bought an outboard and you don’t know how to keep it alive? Hire me before it dies of embarrassment.”

characters.name: Tomas Reyes
characters.desc: “Forty years on this roof. Take me somewhere the fish haven’t heard of me.”

characters.name: Kai
characters.desc: “Eleven days on that raft. I saw you coming from six miles out. I see everything.”

characters.name: Mara Okonkwo
characters.desc: “I charted every roof in Old Meridian. For a share of the haul I’ll chart them for you.”

characters.name: Bram Steele
characters.desc: “Rustfang took my boat and left me tied to a lamppost. I know where they keep the good stuff.”

characters.name: Ines Ferro
characters.desc: “Show me a harpoon and I’ll show you a quiet voyage.”

progression.name: Refine Fuel
progression.desc: Settle, skim, filter, pray. Two crude makes one can of fuel.

progression.name: Hull Patch Kit
progression.desc: Repairs 35 hull anywhere on the water.

progression.name: Alloy Plate
progression.desc: Beat flat, rivet, repeat. Needed for armour and the Ironwake.

progression.name: Engine Parts
progression.desc: Rebuild a carburettor from three broken ones.

progression.name: Stitch Sailcloth
progression.desc: Tarp, twine and patience make passable sailcloth.

progression.name: Strip Wire
progression.desc: Pull the copper out of a dead board.

progression.name: Gold Doubloon
progression.desc: Heavy, slightly bent, and stamped with a king nobody remembers.

progression.name: Silver Piece-of-Eight
progression.desc: Cut into eight wedges for making change. Somebody got shortchanged.

progression.name: Oil-Stained Pearl
progression.desc: Grey-pink and nearly round. The oysters taste of diesel, but they still make these.

progression.name: Signet Ring
progression.desc: Engraved with a leaping fish. Far too big for any finger you own.

progression.name: Sea Emerald
progression.desc: A green stone that seems to hold a little bit of the ocean inside it.

progression.name: Lightkeeper’s Gold Bar
progression.desc: Stamped with a lighthouse. Lightkeepers were paid better than you thought.

progression.name: Carved Turtle Idol
progression.desc: Green stone, worn smooth by hands and tides. The turtle seems to be smiling.

progression.name: Clay Bird Whistle
progression.desc: Blow into it and every gull in earshot turns to look.

progression.name: Sunburst Mask
progression.desc: Hammered gold with eyes of polished shell. It was not made for a human face.

progression.name: Redfinch’s Journal Page
progression.desc: “Day 41. The lighthouse keeper owes me a debt. I have hidden half the chart where only the tide can read it.”

progression.name: Tattered Jolly Flag
progression.desc: The flag of the trawler Wren, Captain Redfinch’s salvage boat. More hole than flag, but unmistakable.

progression.name: Bleached Conch
progression.desc: Hold it to your ear. Yes, it’s the ocean. It’s always the ocean.

progression.name: Spiral Shell
progression.desc: A tidy little staircase someone used to live in.

progression.name: Sand Dollar
progression.desc: Not accepted as currency. You checked.

progression.name: Dried Starfish
progression.desc: Dried and harmless. Has five arms and zero opinions.

progression.name: Sea Glass
progression.desc: A bottle that took fifty years to become a gem.

progression.name: Dead Coral Branch
progression.desc: White as bone. The reefs died with the cities; this is what is left of them.

progression.name: Bronze Ship’s Bell
progression.desc: Engraved “WREN”. Still rings, if a little sadly.

progression.name: Brass Spyglass
progression.desc: The lens is cracked, so everything looks like two of itself.

progression.name: Navigator’s Sextant
progression.desc: For measuring the angle between the sun and your bad decisions.

progression.name: Barnacled Key
progression.desc: Opens something, somewhere. Probably not anything nearby. Probably.

progression.name: Two-Headed Coin
progression.desc: Both sides show the same face. The face is winking.

progression.name: Unsent Letter
progression.desc: “Dear Mum, the island is lovely, the parrot is not.”

progression.name: Stopped Gold Watch
progression.desc: Stopped at 4:17. Everybody’s watch stopped at 4:17, the day the sea came in.

progression.name: Engagement Diamond
progression.desc: Someone said yes. The sea said no.

progression.name: Chart of the Last Summit
progression.desc: Pinned under glass at the top of the Meridian Spire: a chart to a mountain that might still be dry.

progression.name: “Songs for Dry Days” LP
progression.desc: Warped into a gentle saddle. Track four is about rain. Nobody laughs at it any more.

progression.name: Photograph of Dry Land
progression.desc: A family on grass. Actual grass, all the way to the edge of the picture.

progression.name: Helios Crew Badge
progression.desc: “HELIOS PRODUCTION · 2,000 DAYS WITHOUT INCIDENT.” The counter stopped.

progression.name: Transistor Radio
progression.desc: Dry it out, give it a battery, and it hisses. Some nights the hiss sounds like a voice.

progression.name: Meridian Ave. Sign
progression.desc: Pried off a lamppost forty feet underwater. Traffic was lighter than expected.

progression.name: Traffic Light
progression.desc: Stuck on amber forever. Proceed with caution.

progression.name: Ship in a Bottle
progression.desc: From the captain’s cabin of the Meridian Star. A ship, in a bottle, in a ship, in the sea.

progression.name: Sealed Seed Packet
progression.desc: “Heirloom Tomato. Plant after last frost.” Frost. Imagine.

progression.name: Snow Globe
progression.desc: A tiny city under tiny snow. The city is dry. The snow is the only weather.

progression.name: Rubber Duck
progression.desc: The only species that thrived.

progression.name: Algae Mat
progression.desc: Slimy, salty and alive. Pressed and dried it feeds fish, fires and the very poor.

progression.name: Sea-Lettuce Scrap
progression.desc: A green rag of weed peeled off a drowned wall. People eat it. People are hungry.

progression.name: Seedling in a Tin
progression.desc: Two leaves in a bean can of real soil. Somebody watered this with their own ration.

progression.name: Live Moss
progression.desc: A green cushion from the shaded side of the lighthouse. It drinks the fog and keeps it.

progression.name: Jar of Dry Earth
progression.desc: Real dirt: brown, crumbling, full of tiny living things. Traders weigh it on gold scales.

progression.name: Potted Green
progression.desc: A healthy, leafy plant in a blue bucket. People will stop you on the dock just to look at it.

progression.name: Flowers Under Glass
progression.desc: Yellow and white blooms in a sealed jar. Nobody born after the Water has smelled a flower outdoors.

progression.name: Fruiting Tomato Vine
progression.desc: Six red tomatoes on a staked vine in an oil drum. Worth a boat. Worth a fight.

progression.name: Living Tree Sapling
progression.desc: A lemon sapling from the last tree on Canopy Rise, caged in wire. Plant it and in ten years you have shade. Nobody has had shade in sixty.

progression.name: Driftwood
progression.desc: Sun-bleached timber. The shipwright always wants more.

progression.name: Salvaged Rope
progression.desc: Still strong. Smells strongly of seaweed.

progression.name: Iron Nails
progression.desc: Rusty, but a shipwright can straighten anything.

progression.name: Sailcloth Scrap
progression.desc: Torn from a sail that saw better days.

progression.name: Scrap Metal
progression.desc: Rusty plate, bent rebar, a hubcap. Everything floating is a part of something.

progression.name: Copper Wire
progression.desc: Stripped from drowned walls. Mechanics pay well for it.

progression.name: Salvaged Plastic
progression.desc: It will outlive us all. Might as well make it useful.

progression.name: Circuit Boards
progression.desc: Green boards, gold traces. Radar won’t build itself.

progression.name: Crude Oil
progression.desc: Black, thick and precious. Refine it on a workbench into fuel.

progression.name: Fuel Can
progression.desc: Twenty units of go. Use it from the Ship screen to fill your tank.

progression.name: Engine Parts
progression.desc: Pistons, gaskets, a carburettor that still smells of petrol.

progression.name: Alloy Plate
progression.desc: Hammered and riveted scrap. Hulls, armour and pride.

progression.name: Hull Patch Kit
progression.desc: Plank, plastic and pitch. Repairs 35 hull from the Ship screen.

progression.name: Silverfin
progression.desc: Caught by your Fisher. Everyone in every settlement will buy fish.

progression.name: X Marks the Spot
progression.desc: Dig up your first buried treasure chest.

progression.name: Beachcomber
progression.desc: Catalog 5 different Ocean Finds.

progression.name: Wreck Raider
progression.desc: Recover 3 different Shipwreck items.

progression.name: Curiouser
progression.desc: Catalog 3 different Curiosities.

progression.name: Amateur Archaeologist
progression.desc: Catalog 3 Ancient Artifacts.

progression.name: Ten Discoveries
progression.desc: Catalog 10 different discoveries.

progression.name: Twenty Discoveries
progression.desc: Catalog 20 different discoveries.

progression.name: Scavenger
progression.desc: Haul up 10 loads of salvage.

progression.name: Under the Flare
progression.desc: Dock at Rig Helios.

progression.name: Through the Wall
progression.desc: Reach the Meridian Spire inside the Stormwall.

progression.name: Archivist of the Drowned
progression.desc: Catalog 30 different discoveries.

progression.desc: Salvage the Sunken Tower

progression.desc: Install a Salvaged Outboard

progression.desc: Recruit your first crew member

progression.desc: Commission the Scrap Trimaran

progression.name: g_helios
progression.desc: Reach Rig Helios

progression.name: g_meridian
progression.desc: Salvage Old Meridian

progression.name: g_raiders
progression.desc: Drive off a Rustfang raider

progression.name: g_ironwake
progression.desc: Build the Ironwake Expedition Cat

progression.name: g_spire
progression.desc: Pierce the Stormwall: reach the Meridian Spire

progression.name: g_done
progression.desc: Find the Last Summit

progression.name: Patchwork Skiff
progression.desc: Eight planks, a car bonnet and a sail stitched from a billboard. Floats out of habit.

progression.name: Scrap Trimaran
progression.desc: A real deck, a keel, and two outrigger floats welded from fuel tanks. Built to cross the open swell to the Sunken Reach.

progression.name: Ironwake Expedition Cat
progression.desc: Twin armoured hulls under a working deck the size of a house. The only boat in the Drift built to go through the Stormwall.

progression.name: Canvas Mainsail
progression.desc: A proper sail on a proper yard. 40% faster, and it doesn’t have a hole shaped like a seagull.

progression.name: Cutter Rig + Jib
progression.desc: Adds a jib up front. Catches the wind from more angles. 70% faster than stock.

progression.name: Salvaged Outboard
progression.desc: A two-stroke that coughs, then roars. Tap ENGINE to motor anywhere, wind or no wind. Burns fuel.

progression.name: Twin Diesel Drive
progression.desc: Two diesels pulled from a harbour tug. Outruns raiders and storms. Only Rig Helios can fit one.

progression.name: Copper-Banded Hull
progression.desc: Copper sheathing along the waterline. Lets you scrape over the reef breakers around Gull Shoal. +20 hull.

progression.name: Riveted Armour Plating
progression.desc: Alloy plate bolted over the hull. Storms and raider rams do 45% less damage. +60 hull.

progression.name: Lashed Cargo Crate
progression.desc: A sturdy crate lashed to the stern. +4 cargo slots.

progression.name: Rope Cargo Nets
progression.desc: Nets slung along the sides for bulky finds. +8 cargo slots total.

progression.name: Fuel Drum Rack
progression.desc: Four lashed drums. +60 fuel capacity. Go further, come back.

progression.name: Ash-Wood Rudder
progression.desc: A bigger blade and a tiller with a grip. Turns 45% sharper.

progression.name: Brass Compass
progression.desc: Mounted on the bow. Points toward the X on whichever treasure map you’re following.

progression.name: Salvage Radar
progression.desc: A spinning dish on a lattice mast. Pings salvage sites and drifting caches within 420 m.

progression.name: Salvage Crane & Winch
progression.desc: Hydraulic boom and a drum winch. Lifts heavy salvage (tankers, rigs, the Spire) and widens your winch window.

progression.name: Harpoon Turret
progression.desc: A pneumatic harpoon on a swivel. Raiders that come close get a very pointed warning.

progression.name: Solar Array
progression.desc: Four cracked panels and a charge controller. Trickles 2.5 fuel a minute back into the tank by day.

progression.name: Deck Wind Turbine
progression.desc: Spins day and night. With the solar array: 6 fuel a minute, more in a storm.

progression.name: Container Cabin
progression.desc: Half a shipping container with bunks, a porthole and a tomato plant. +2 crew berths.

progression.name: String Lights & Spotlight
progression.desc: Warm bulbs along the rail and a spotlight on the bow. Your boat glows at night and caches glint in the dark.

progression.name: Trolling Rods
progression.desc: Two rods off the stern. Catch Silverfin while you sail. A Fisher on the crew triples the catch.

levelcraft.title: LEVELCRAFT

findings.title: 53% of the mapped area holds nothing to find or do
findings.summary: Dividing the playable extent (1125×1800 units) into a 6×6 grid, 19 cells contain no placed location and no mission target; the emptiest quarter is the north-west (6 of 9 cells empty).
findings.why: Players read empty space as either a promise or a waste. Without a landmark, a cache or a reason to cross it, a large empty area becomes travel time between the parts of the game that matter.

evidence.text: 58 positioned locations and targets; 19 empty grid cells
evidence.symbol: positions across ISLANDS, OUTPOSTS, POIS, SALVAGE_SITES, SETTLEMENTS

strengths: 29 kinds of place across 59 named locations (variety 0.91).
The world is organised into 3 regions: shallows (7), emerald (7), stormwall (1).

missioncraft.title: MISSIONCRAFT
missioncraft.note: No mission, quest or job definitions were found as data. 1 guided step chain(s) were found and are assessed by ExperienceCraft (onboarding).

findings.title: 14 named characters are barely present in the writing
findings.summary: Juno Vale, Tomas Reyes, Kai, Mara Okonkwo and 10 more are defined as characters but appear in at most one authored line and never speak.
findings.why: A named character the player meets once is set dressing with a name tag. Each one is an unpaid promise of a relationship.

progressioncraft.title: PROGRESSIONCRAFT
strengths: 8 unlocks have prerequisites, so progression has structure beyond price.
Replay sources: randomness (530), procedural (43), best scores (140), seeded (19).

findings.title: The guided chain First Voyage is 13 steps long
findings.summary: First Voyage walks the player through 13 sequential steps (Learn to steer, Sail out of Driftholm, Sail to the atoll to the west, Drop anchor near the beach…).
findings.why: A long, strictly ordered tutorial delays the moment the player chooses for themselves. Most players decide whether they like a game in that window.

findings.title: PLAYCRAFT measured 8.6 s from load to first input
findings.summary: In PLAYCRAFT run 20261105001617-pass-7fe56aea the game took 8.6 s before it accepted play (software renderer; real devices are usually faster).
findings.why: The first seconds decide whether a mobile player stays. Anything between tap and play should be part of the experience, not a wait.

findings.summary: In PLAYCRAFT run 20261105001617-pass-7fe56aea the game took 8.6 s before it accepted play (software renderer; real devices are usually faster).
findings.why: The first seconds decide whether a mobile player stays. Anything between tap and play should be part of the experience, not a wait.

findings.title: 53% of the mapped area holds nothing to find or do
findings.summary: Dividing the playable extent (1125×1800 units) into a 6×6 grid, 19 cells contain no placed location and no mission target; the emptiest quarter is the north-west (6 of 9 cells empty).
findings.why: Players read empty space as either a promise or a waste. Without a landmark, a cache or a reason to cross it, a large empty area becomes travel time between the parts of the game that matter.

proposals.label: A · Conservative
proposals.proposal: Give Juno Vale, Tomas Reyes and Kai a voice: one line each where the player meets them, one more later.
changes: Write 2 lines per character tied to existing missions or places.
Have each say something only they would say (their job, their worry).
proposals.experience: Names become people; players start to recognise them.

validation.metric: characters with ≥ 2 mentions and a line
validation.method: STORYCRAFT re-run; playtest: name three characters.

proposals.existing: Juno Vale, Tomas Reyes, Kai, Mara Okonkwo and 10 more are defined as characters but appear in at most one authored line and never speak.
proposals.problem: 14 named characters are barely present in the writing
proposals.why: A named character the player meets once is set dressing with a name tag. Each one is an unpaid promise of a relationship.

proposals.label: B · Ambitious
proposals.proposal: Build a small arc around one of them (Juno Vale).
changes: Three beats across the campaign: Juno Vale asks, Juno Vale is in trouble, Juno Vale pays it back.
Attach each beat to a mission the player already plays.
proposals.experience: A relationship that develops over hours; the payoff lands because the player was there for the setup.

validation.method: STORYCRAFT re-run; playtest emotional rating at the payoff.

proposals.label: A · Conservative
proposals.proposal: Cut First Voyage to its first five steps; teach the rest in context.
changes: Keep steering, the first goal and the first reward; move the rest to just-in-time hints.

validation.method: EXPERIENCECRAFT re-run; PLAYCRAFT time to first free choice.

proposals.existing: First Voyage walks the player through 13 sequential steps (Learn to steer, Sail out of Driftholm, Sail to the atoll to the west, Drop anchor near the beach…).
proposals.problem: The guided chain First Voyage is 13 steps long
proposals.why: A long, strictly ordered tutorial delays the moment the player chooses for themselves. Most players decide whether they like a game in that window.

proposals.label: A · Conservative
proposals.proposal: Add landmarks and small finds to the north-west of the map.
changes: Place 2–3 visible landmarks in the north-west quarter on lines players already travel.
Put one small reward at each (a collectible, a view, a line of lore).
proposals.experience: Crossing the area becomes a sequence of small discoveries instead of empty travel.
tradeoffs: Adds rendering cost in that area.

validation.method: LEVELCRAFT re-run; playtest: ask players to sketch the map from memory.
